name: DEEPWELL DRIFT: Communal Dream Space Network
description: A network of communal dream parlors operating in Tier 2 basement venues, offering group BCI-linked sleep sessions where 4–12 participants share a loosely synchronized dreamspace constructed from blended contributors' subconscious imagery. Unlike clinical shared dreaming systems, DEEPWELL DRIFT uses open-architecture BCI bridging software that allows genuine unfiltered cross-contamination between dreamers — the resulting spaces are unpredictable, collaborative, and often profoundly strange. Sessions run 3–6 hours, with participants sleeping in proximity on reclining racks.
story_hooks: A regular DEEPWELL DRIFT group begins collectively dreaming a location none of them have visited — a room that, when described to an urban archaeologist, matches a sealed section of Old Chicago infrastructure.
One participant in a group session appears to have died during the dream but their BCI is still transmitting, and their signal is reshaping the shared dreamspace around the other sleepers.

A corponation intelligence operative has been attending sessions under a false identity, using the open BCI bridging to harvest subconscious operational data from participants who work in sensitive infrastructure roles.
